newsitem.title: USA: Stubborn storm floods mid-Atlantic U.S. states.
newsitem.headline: Stubborn storm floods mid-Atlantic U.S. states.

text.p: Steady rains that have soaked the mid-Atlantic region for nearly a week eased briefly Tuesday, but a stubborn storm system continued to linger over the region, officials said.
"There's a possibility of rain every day this week," West Virginia emergency management spokesman Clay Carney said.
Several inches of rain have caused localised flooding from western Ohio to Maryland, pushing up rivers and streams and driving hundreds of people from their homes.
Flood watches were in effect in Ohio, Virginia and Maryland, the National Weather Service said.
In West Virginia on Sunday evening, a 34-year-old woman and her neighbour, a 15-year-old boy, on their way back from church were swept away by a flash flood and drowned, Carney said.

The western Ohio county of Putnam asked for state assistance after the Blanchard River spilled out of its banks, and a half-dozen other counties were also threatened, a spokeswoman for Ohio's Emergency Management Agency said.
The steady showers were caused by a stalled low-pressure system centred over Georgia that continued to spin storms through the mid-Atlantic region.

"It's like an eddy," said Joe Olson, a meteorologist with the Weather Service's Hazardous Storm Centre. "It's out of the main stream, where there's nothing to act on it to get it to move. So its sitting there spinning, bringing in moisture from the Gulf (of Mexico) and the Atlantic."
The storm was expected to gradually move up the eastern seaboard beginning Wednesday.
